name: Large sets with Property P
description: construct() -> a nonempty subset of [1,n=256]. For every a<b<=c in the set, a must NOT divide b+c. Repeated larger summands b=c are included. Maximize cardinality. Finite cardinality maximization in [1,256], including repeated larger summands. The cited work proves the extremal bound for sufficiently large n; this task claims neither novelty nor its applicability threshold at 256.

state_of_the_art.statement: The maximum is 86 = floor(256/3) + 1, attained by {171, ..., 256}. An exact integer programme (151,333 divisibility constraints, solved to optimality with HiGHS; scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py --slow) shows that no larger subset of [1,256] has the property. Bedert proved the bound floor(n/3) + 1 for all sufficiently large n, as conjectured by Erdős and Sárközy.
